families_added.scope: A pre-registered, frozen-decision-rule adversarial audit of six prior generative-falsification family claims: (1) discovery and quantification that the shared corpus parser used by prior pilots leaves IVTFF markup inside ~24% of published types, requiring restatement of all headline manuscript metrics under a newly implemented clean parser (with two uncertain-space treatment variants); (2) an alphabet-confound test showing the H2|1 anomaly is robust to EVA multigraph/determinism-merge alphabet normalization but the final-glyph anomaly is alphabet-dependent (0.08-0.27 bit gap depending on glyph-identity assumptions); (3) five untuned cipher constructions applied to real Latin/Culpeper plaintexts, showing a plain verbose cipher of Latin reproduces both entropy residues and fails only a type-ratio gate calibrated to the contaminated parser count; (4) permutation-null and Currier-language/section confound analysis showing the 'neighbouring-page 2x sharing' and '30% page-private' structural claims are largely artefacts of language/section confounding and hapax richness; (5) a new medieval-orthography control (two Chaucer editions) testing whether the vocabulary-richness anomaly survives non-standardized spelling.

family_comparisons.existing_scope: Pilot 4 in the generative-mechanism falsification family: implements the Cardan table-and-grille device (M5a independent-column, M5b row-coupled) built from the pinned ZL3b corpus, measures composite distance against real manuscript statistics across 28 configurations plus multi-seed stability, and narrows the residual gap to two local metrics (conditional bigram entropy, word-final predictability), extending outcome-m4-template-doodler-pilot.
family_comparisons.reason: This submission does not build or test a new generative device model; it audits the shared parser and re-tests structural/content claims via ciphers, alphabet confounds and permutation nulls. family_comparisons.existing_scope: A distinct generative-mechanism falsification pilot implementing Stolfi's published 2000 word grammar (core/mantle/crust unimodal-hill slot structure) as a template generator embedded in an entry/topic-carryover engine, and measuring two real-language positive controls (Culpeper's Complete Herbal 1653, Alice in Wonderland) with the identical metric suite against the pinned ZL3b corpus across 12 grid variants, showing (a) real language differs from the manuscript on conditional entropy, final-char entropy and entry-private vocabulary share, reframing prior 'unmatched by content-free generators' results away from a linguistic-content reading, and (b) the published grammar covers 86% of corpus word types with zero fitting and jointly reproduces vocabulary size, ttr, word length and page-sharing, leaving a residual mechanical-repetition signature (H2|1, final-char entropy, Zipf slope, entry-unique overshoot).
family_comparisons.reason: Reuses Culpeper/Alice bytes as baseline inputs for new cipher/orthography tests; does not implement or claim the word-grammar template generator or its coverage-percentage finding.

family_comparisons.existing_scope: A bounded diagnostic control extending the existing entry-structure metric suite (entry-private vocabulary share, adjacent/distant page Jaccard, ttr, entry token length) to two new real-text genres (Devil's Dictionary, Wonder Book of Knowledge) alongside the previously measured Culpeper/Alice controls, showing the manuscript's entry-private vocabulary is genre- and entry-length-dependent and lies on a continuum with short-entry real genres rather than being an order-of-magnitude outlier, with a documented correction to an earlier interpretive emphasis about device-overshoot.
family_comparisons.reason: Does not add new genre controls; instead re-derives page-jaccard/page-unique metrics using permutation nulls and language/section confound partitioning on a newly cleaned parser -- a different diagnostic instrument and different genre scope.

family_comparisons.existing_scope: A new bounded diagnostic control in the generative-falsification research area: measures line-structured metrics (word-final char entropy, line-final word final-char entropy, line-initial first-char entropy, top-5 line-final word rhyme concentration) across the pinned ZL3b corpus's real lines, a newly added rhymed-verse control (Shakespeare's Sonnets, PG 1041), and existing Culpeper/Alice prose pseudo-line baselines, showing that rhyme (even at its most ending-constrained, 3.50 bits) does not approach the manuscript's every-word final-char entropy (2.59 bits), excluding versification as the mechanism behind the residual word-ending discipline, plus a side finding that the manuscript's line-final position is less constrained than its average word (2.99 vs 2.59), opposite of rhyme.
family_comparisons.reason: No line/rhyme metrics used here; unrelated mechanism and evidence base.

family_comparisons.existing_scope: A bounded diagnostic control extending the generative-falsification metric suite (final-glyph entropy, conditional bigram entropy H2|1, type/token diversity, word length) to nine same-text (Bible) translations at equal 35k-token samples, testing whether a morphologically rich real language naturally reproduces the manuscript's word-ending discipline. Finds no tested language reaches the manuscript on either final-glyph entropy or H2|1; Finnish is nearest on endings (2.80 vs 2.58) but not close on H2|1; Russian, despite rich inflection, has the least predictable endings, refuting a simple morphology-based explanation; manuscript retains highest type diversity of all ten texts.
